**What I found**
Don't build the plugin registry yet (the record calls this DROP). JSON is the only format, nobody has asked for a second one, and no third party has been named. All three commands (`export`, `report`, `print`) call one 3-line function, `toJson` in `src/format/json.js:1`. A registry with a single formatter is an abstraction with one implementation, so the proposal fails the necessity check before its worth is even scored.

**Why it matters**
Building it adds a new module, an extra dependency hop for every command, a plugin-loading path that runs third-party code, and a `--format` option the CLI doesn't have today (`src/cli.js:9`). A plugin API is also a public contract: once outside code depends on it, you can't change it freely. If you don't build it, nothing breaks. If a second format is ever needed, adding it as an internal formatter takes about one file and one flag.

**Do this first**
1. Leave `src/format/json.js` and the three commands as they are. Close the proposal with this record so it doesn't come back without new evidence.
2. Follow-up, only if a concrete request for a second format arrives: add `src/format/<name>.js` and a `--format` flag that picks between two built-in functions. Re-run `/alchemy` when a third format or a named outside plugin author shows up.

**What I did not check**
- Requirements grounding did not run. The request has no named user or problem behind it, and the absence of demand already settles M. Closing it would mean running `/alchemy` again with any real request for a format.
- I didn't check issue trackers, support tickets or roadmap docs for format requests; none are in this repo. "Nobody has asked" is your statement. A search of your tracker for "format", "csv", "yaml" or "plugin" would close this.
- No tests or lint ran, because no code changed.
